note: An intermediate guitar week at 30 minutes a day: joining pentatonic positions is the key skill and returns on five days in new forms (position 2, position 3, a new key, bends across the join, from memory), with legato and picking warm-ups, sus and add9 parts over a strum-along, chord tones and a melody up the neck. Each step says what to press and where to look.

plan.title: Week 1: beyond position 1
plan.summary: Join the A minor pentatonic positions 1 to 3, bend and slide across the joins, and use sus chords, chord tones and a melody to keep it musical.

exercises.title: Hammer and pull
exercises.focus: Legato trill · fingers 1-3 · G string, 5th fret
exercises.why: Hammer-ons and pull-offs let notes flow without picking, and they build the strength the joins need.

sections.text: Put finger 1 on the 5th fret of the G string and finger 3 on the 7th. Press Play below to start the metronome. Pick the 5th fret once. Then, without picking again, hammer finger 3 onto the 7th fret and pull it off back to the 5th, one note per beat. Keep both notes equally loud.

exercises.title: D, Dsus2, Dsus4
exercises.focus: Sus colours on D · strummed at 80 bpm
exercises.why: Sus chords move one finger off and back on, which turns a plain chord into a moving part.

sections.text: The three shapes
Press a chord box to hear it. From D, lift your finger off the high E string: that is Dsus2. Put your pinky on the 3rd fret of the high E: that is Dsus4. Switch between them slowly, in any order.
As a groove
Press Play below; the lit block shows the chord. Strum along, one bar each. Keep the strumming hand moving. Change only the one finger.

exercises.title: Position 1 to position 2
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · positions 1 → 2 · 70 then 80 bpm
exercises.why: One slide on the G string is all it takes to leave position 1 behind.

sections.text: Position 2 on its own
Play position 2 up and down at your own pace. It starts at the 7th fret. Its ringed {{1}} notes are on the D and B strings.
Cross on the G string
Climb position 1. On the G string, slide from {{4}} (D, 7th fret) up to {{5}} (E, 9th fret). Finish the climb in position 2. Come back down the same way.
At 80
Press Play below to start the metronome. Play the same crossing at 80. Land the slide right on a click.

exercises.title: Improvise across the join
exercises.focus: Positions 1-2 over Am7-Dm7
exercises.why: Using the join in a solo is what makes it stick.

sections.text: Land on the roots
Press Play below to start the backing and improvise in positions 1 and 2. Cross between them once in each phrase. Land on {{a}} when Am7 comes round and on {{d}} when Dm7 comes round.
Start in position 2
Same backing. Now start each phrase in position 2. End it in position 1.

exercises.title: Alternate picking
exercises.focus: Down-up, four notes per string, 90 bpm
exercises.why: Strict down-up picking keeps fast lines even.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Pick four notes per string, down-up-down-up, one note per beat. Go across all six strings and back. Keep the pick motion small.

exercises.title: Cadd9 to Dsus4
exercises.focus: Cadd9-G-Dsus4-Em at 80 bpm
exercises.why: Cadd9, G and Dsus4 share the same two fingers on the top strings, so the changes ring into each other.

sections.text: Anchor fingers
Press a chord box to hear it. Keep fingers 3 and 4 on the 3rd fret of the B and high E strings for Cadd9, G and Dsus4. Move only the bass fingers. Lift the two top fingers for Em.
In time
Press Play below; the lit block shows the chord. Strum along, one bar per chord. Keep the top fingers down through the changes.

exercises.title: Bends in tune
exercises.focus: Whole-step bends in position 1 · D to E, G to A
exercises.why: A bend is only good if it lands on a real note, so always check it against the note you aim for.

sections.text: G string: D up to E
Play {{5}} (E, 9th fret of the G string) to hear the target. Then bend {{4}} (D, 7th fret) up a whole step until it matches. Switch between the target and the bend.
B string: G up to A
Now the B string. Play {{1}} (A, 10th fret), then bend {{b7}} (G, 8th fret) up to it. Hold the bend. Pick the {{1}} on the high E (5th fret) against it.

exercises.title: Slow blues phrases
exercises.focus: Bends in A over drums and bass, 70 bpm
exercises.why: A slow tempo leaves room for each bend to ring out, and this is the scale the blues uses.

sections.text: One bend per phrase
Press Play below to start the band. Play short phrases in positions 1 and 2. Put one bend in each: {{4}} up to {{5}}, or {{b7}} up to {{1}}. Leave a bar of space after each phrase.
Slide into the join
Now start each phrase with the slide from position 1 into position 2. End it with a bend. Record a minute and listen back.

exercises.title: Legato, fingers 2-4
exercises.focus: Legato trill · fingers 2-4 · B string, 7th fret
exercises.why: Fingers 2 and 4 are the weaker pair, and position 3 needs them.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Pick once, then hammer finger 4 and pull off to finger 2, one note per beat. Rest when the hand gets tired, then go again.

exercises.title: Chord tones over Am-F-C-G
exercises.focus: 1-3-5 of each chord · play-along in the neck view
exercises.why: Playing each chord's own notes as it passes trains you to hear the changes in a solo.

sections.text: Slow, in the neck view
Press Play below and play the lit note, one per beat: each chord's root, 3rd, 5th, 3rd. Am has a minor 3rd ({{b3}}). F, C and G have major 3rds.
Faster, from tab
Press Play below for the same line at 80, now reading the tab.

exercises.title: Position 2 to position 3
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · positions 2 → 3
exercises.why: Position 3 carries the line up to the 13th fret, and its join is a slide on the B string.

sections.text: Position 3 on its own
Press Play above to start the metronome. Play position 3 up and down, one note per beat. Find every {{1}} in it first.
Cross on the B string
Climb position 2. On the B string, slide from {{b7}} (G, 8th fret) up to {{1}} (A, 10th fret). Finish in position 3. Come back down the same way.
Three positions in one run
Start low in position 1. Cross into position 2 on the G string, then into position 3 on the B string. Then go all the way back down.

exercises.title: Three-position solo
exercises.focus: Positions 1-3 over Am7-Dm7, 85 bpm
exercises.why: A solo that climbs through the positions builds like a story.

sections.text: Low to high
Press Play below to start the backing. Start in position 1. Move up one position every four bars. Land on {{a}} when Am7 comes round and on {{d}} when Dm7 comes round.
High to low
Same backing. Now start in position 3. Come down one position every four bars.

exercises.title: Picking across strings
exercises.focus: Down-up, two notes per string, 100 bpm
exercises.why: Two notes per string makes the pick cross strings on every upstroke, the hardest move for picking.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Pick two notes per string, down-up, across all six strings and back.

exercises.title: Sus groove in D
exercises.focus: D-Dsus4-Dsus2 with bass-and-chord picking
exercises.why: Picking the bass note and then the chord makes three shapes sound like a whole arrangement.

sections.text: Bass, then chord
Press Play below; the lit block shows the chord, one bar each. Pick the open D string on beats 1 and 3. Strum the top strings on beats 2 and 4.
Add G and A
Press a chord box to hear it. Then press Play for D, G, A, D with the same picking. Try a sus4 on the last beat of a bar where it fits.

exercises.title: Legato in the position
exercises.focus: Hammer-ons and pull-offs in position 1 of A
exercises.why: Legato inside the scale turns runs into smooth phrases.

sections.text: One trill
Trill fingers 1 and 3 on the G string at the 5th fret: C to D. Pick only the first note.
Through the position
Climb position 1. Pick the first note on each string and hammer on the second. Come down with pull-offs. Start and end on the low {{1}}.

exercises.title: A tune to the high Do
exercises.focus: A Ti-stage tune in D with eighth notes, up the neck
exercises.why: A tune that climbs past the octave makes you shift position mid-phrase.

sections.text: Learn it slowly
Press Play to hear it. The tune climbs from Sol to the high Do, with a quick La-Ti-La-Sol in the middle. Play along from the tab, one phrase at a time.
On the neck at tempo
Now in the neck view, a little faster. Play it higher up the neck, with no open strings.

exercises.title: Cadd9-G-Dsus4-Em, faster
exercises.focus: Anchor-finger changes at 90 bpm
exercises.why: The same anchor fingers from day 2, now as a warm-up at a faster tempo.

sections.text: Press Play below; the lit block shows the chord. Strum along, one bar per chord. Keep fingers 3 and 4 on the top strings until Em.

exercises.title: G minor pentatonic, positions 1 to 3
exercises.focus: Positions 1 → 2 → 3 in G, from the 3rd fret
exercises.why: Moving the joins to a new key shows you know the shapes, not the frets.

sections.text: Position 1 at the 3rd fret
G minor pentatonic position 1 starts at the 3rd fret, two frets lower than A. Play it up and down, starting on the {{1}}.
Both joins
The joins are the same as in A. Slide {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string into position 2. Slide {{b7}} to {{1}} on the B string into position 3.
At 80
Press Play below to start the metronome. Run all three positions up and back at 80.

exercises.title: Gm arpeggio in two positions
exercises.focus: G minor arpeggio · positions 1-2
exercises.why: The arpeggio is the skeleton inside the scale: the notes that sound safe over Gm.

sections.text: Position 1
Press Play above to start the metronome. Play {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}} up and down in position 1, one note per beat.
Across positions 1 and 2
Now across both positions. Cross where they share a note. Then play only the {{b3}} in each position: the note that makes the chord minor.

exercises.title: Solo in G
exercises.focus: Positions 1-3 of G minor pentatonic over Gm7-Cm7
exercises.why: Aiming at the arpeggio's notes while moving through the positions joins today's two skills.

sections.text: Aim at the chord
Press Play below to start the backing. Land on {{g}} or {{b-flat}} when Gm7 comes round and on {{c}} when Cm7 comes round.
Use all three positions
Same backing. Use all three positions. Cross a join in every phrase.

exercises.title: Skip a string
exercises.focus: Down-up string skipping, 80 bpm
exercises.why: Skipping a string makes the pick hand jump accurately, which wide phrases need.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Pick two notes per string, down-up, skipping a string each time: low E, D, B, then back. Keep the skipped strings quiet.

exercises.title: Em-Cadd9-G-Dsus4 in sixteenths
exercises.focus: Sixteenth strumming at 70 bpm
exercises.why: Sixteenths double the hand's motion, so the groove stays tight at a slow tempo.

sections.text: On Em only
Press a chord box to hear it. On Em, strum down-up-down-up on every beat. Accent beats 2 and 4.
Over the changes
Press Play below; the lit block shows the chord. Keep the sixteenths going, one bar per chord.

exercises.title: Slide in, bend out
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · join 1 → 2 with a bend to finish
exercises.why: A slide into position 2 followed by a bend is a classic lead move, and it uses both joins of the week.

sections.text: The lick slowly
Press Play above to start the metronome. Slide {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string. Play {{b7}} (G, 8th fret) on the B string. Bend it up to {{1}}, then release. The whole lick takes four clicks.
In position 3 too
Now move it up. Slide {{b7}} to {{1}} on the B string into position 3. Then bend {{4}} up to {{5}} on the high E string (D at the 10th fret, up to E).

exercises.title: The tune, at tempo
exercises.focus: Day 4's tune in D at 90 bpm
exercises.why: Coming back to the tune two days later shows what stuck.

sections.text: From memory
Play the tune once without the app. Then press Play and check it.
Faster and with a slide
Press Play below to play it faster, sliding into the high Do instead of picking it.

exercises.title: Legato check
exercises.focus: Trills 1-3 and 2-4 at 90 bpm
exercises.why: The week's legato at a faster tempo, to hear the progress.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Trill fingers 1 and 3 on the G string for a minute. Then fingers 2 and 4 on the B string for a minute. How does it feel next to day 1?

exercises.title: Sus part for the jam
exercises.focus: Am7-Dsus2-Dm7 rhythm part
exercises.why: A sus chord between Am7 and Dm7 gives the jam a moving rhythm part.

sections.text: Press a chord box to hear it. Then press Play. The lit block shows the chord, one block per beat: Am7 for a whole bar, then Dsus2 and Dm7 for two beats each.

exercises.title: Three positions from memory
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic positions 1-3 without the chart
exercises.why: The week's key skill without help: the test that it is yours.

sections.text: Without looking
Press Play above to start the metronome. Run positions 1 to 3 and back without looking at the neck below. Then check against it.
In G
Same in G, starting from the 3rd fret. Still without looking.

exercises.title: The jam
exercises.focus: Positions 1-3 with bends and slides over Am7-Dm7
exercises.why: Everything from the week in one solo: joins, bends, legato and chord tones.

sections.text: Chord tones first
Press Play below to start the backing. Land on {{a}} or {{c}} when Am7 comes round and on {{d}} or {{f}} when Dm7 comes round.
Bends and slides
Same backing. Play day 6's slide-and-bend lick in every chorus.
Record it
Record four minutes of soloing. Climb from position 1 to position 3 and back. Listen back and pick one phrase you like for next week.
